question: A Canadian home-maintenance note says “clean the eavestroughs.” Which part of the house does that refer to, and what other common word might a neighbour use?
generated_answer:
The term “eavestroughs” is a Canadian English term for what is commonly known as a “gutter” in American English. It refers to the troughs or channels that collect rainwater from the roof and direct it away from the building, usually through downspouts. The term “eavestroughs” is more commonly used in Canada, while “gutters” is the term used in the United States and many other English-speaking countries.

So, if a Canadian home-maintenance note says “clean the eavestroughs,” it means to clean the gutters. A neighbour might use the term “gutters” instead, which would be understood by Canadians as well, although “eavestroughs” is the more common term in Canada.

In summary, “eavestroughs” refers to the gutters on a house, and a neighbour might use the term “gutters” to refer to the same thing. Both terms are understood in Canada, but “eavestroughs” is more commonly used in Canadian English.
